title: Bichargon Hall Effect
abstract: The conventional Hall effect arises from the transverse deflection of mobile electronic charge carriers in conductors. Here, we predict a bosonic charge Hall effect in charge-ordered insulators mediated by bichargons, collective bosonic excitations of charge order carrying quantized electric charges $\pm 2e$. In contrast to conventional electronic carriers, a thermally excited bichargon gas does not support dc electrical conduction in response to an external electric field despite its constituents carrying finite electric charges. We show that a temperature gradient can instead drive a diffusive flow of thermal bichargons, while an out-of-plane magnetic field deflects the oppositely charged bichargons in opposite transverse directions via the Lorentz force, leading to a finite Hall charge current and opposite charge accumulations at the sample edges. Our results broaden the paradigm of charge Hall transport beyond conventional electronic conductors, establishing that a charge Hall response can emerge in an electrically \emph{insulating} system through charged bosonic quasiparticles.
summary: This work predicts a novel bosonic charge Hall effect in charge-ordered insulators, mediated by collective excitations called bichargons. Unlike conventional conductors, the system remains insulating because the DC current vanishes, but a temperature gradient combined with a magnetic field generates a measurable transverse Hall charge current. This broadens the understanding of charge transport by utilizing charged bosonic quasiparticles.
main_problem: The paper predicts a bosonic charge Hall effect in charge-ordered insulators, extending the concept of charge Hall transport beyond conventional electronic conductors.
main_result: A finite transverse Hall charge current and edge charge accumulation can be generated by a temperature gradient and an out-of-plane magnetic field, even though the system remains electrically insulating.
method: The analysis uses the semi-classical Boltzmann equation applied to the bosonic excitations (bichargons) and calculates the resulting thermoelectric Hall coefficient.
model_or_system: The system is a charge-ordered insulator modeled using the extended Hubbard model on a 2D square lattice. The key excitations are bichargons, bosonic quasiparticles carrying quantized charges of $\pm 2e$.
key_observables: Finite Hall charge current, opposite charge accumulations at sample edges, and the Hall thermoelectric coefficient ($L_{bH}$).

main_assumptions: The analysis employs the relaxation-time approximation for the Boltzmann equation and assumes the bichargon gap ($\Delta_b$) is significantly smaller than the electronic gap ($E_g$).

paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical model using the extended Hubbard Hamiltonian, derives the effective low-energy Hamiltonian for bichargons, and then applies the semi-classical Boltzmann equation to calculate the current response under combined thermal and magnetic fields.
why_interesting: The mechanism relies on bosonic quasiparticles (bichargons) in an insulating state, providing a novel platform for studying charge transport phenomena that bypasses the need for mobile electronic carriers, which is relevant to strongly correlated materials.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic of the bichargon Hall effect in a charge- ordered insulator. Two branches of bichargons carrying oppo- site electric charges ±2e diffuse in the same direction without generating a net longitudinal charge current under an applied temperature gradient, while an out-of-plane magnetic field de- flects them in opposite transverse directions via the Lorentz force, leading to a finite Hall charge current and thereby op- posite charge accumulations at the two lateral edges.

FIG. 2. (a) Checkerboard charge order in the half-filled ex- tended Hubbard model on a two-dimensional square lattice, where the alternating empty |0⟩and doubly occupied |2⟩sites can be mapped onto staggered pseudospin-1/2 order. (b) Two branches of oppositely charged (±2e) bichargons associated with pseudospin-flip excitations, analogous to the two magnon branches in a bipartite antiferromagnet carrying opposite spin angular momenta ±ℏ. The two branches of bichargon exci- tations are energetically degenerate and equally populated in equilibrium, thereby leaving the total electric charge of the system unchanged.
